Methods for fgls fits

Source: R/methods-fgls.R
fgls-methods.Rd

Standard accessors for objects returned by fgls(), serial_fgls(), lasso_fgls() and the benchmark estimators. They make the fits work with generic tools such as lmtest::coeftest() and lmtest::coefci().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
vcov(object, type = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
confint(object, parm, level = 0.95, type = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
residuals(object, type = c("response", "innovations"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  se.fit = FALSE,
  interval = c("none", "confidence"),
  level = 0.95,
  na.action = stats::na.pass,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
df.residual(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
formula(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
model.matrix(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
model.frame(formula, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
terms(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

object, x, formula

An "fgls" object.

type

For vcov() and confint(): NULL (the variance chosen when fitting) or another variance type to compute from the stored estimates: "robust", "naive", "nonrobust", "HC0"–"HC3" (where available) or "bootstrap" (re-runs the estimator). For residuals(): "response" (\(y_t - x_t'\hat\beta\), full sample) or "innovations" (residuals of the final filtered and/or weighted regression).

...

Not used.

parm

Coefficients (names or positions); all by default.

level

Confidence level.

newdata

Optional data frame in which to look for the regressors.

se.fit

Return standard errors of the predicted means.

interval

"none" or "confidence" (for the mean of the response).

na.action

Missing-value handling for newdata.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

The usual values: a coefficient covariance matrix (vcov), a matrix of confidence limits (confint), vectors of residuals or fitted values, predictions (a vector, or a list/matrix with se.fit/interval), or the corresponding model components.

Details

Inference is asymptotically normal (as in the papers) unless the fit was made with use_t = TRUE. Accordingly, df.residual() returns Inf for normal inference, so that lmtest::coeftest() reproduces summary.fgls(), and \(n_{eff} - q\) otherwise. nobs() returns the number of observations in the final regression, \(n_{eff} = T - k^*\).

Variances and the sandwich package

The variance estimators of the papers are available through vcov(fit, type = ...) and can be passed to other tools (for example lmtest::coeftest(fit, vcov. = vcov(fit, type = "naive"))). The package provides no sandwich::estfun() or sandwich::bread() methods, because the robust variance of PG26 eq. (29) and the bias-corrected sandwich of GP24 eq. (8) are not of the generic form those functions assume: sandwich::vcovHAC() and related functions would not reproduce them.

See also

Other fgls: compare_fgls(), fgls(), fgls_control(), lasso_fgls(), plot.fgls(), serial_fgls(), summary.fgls()

Examples

sim <- simulate_serial(200, seed = 1)
fit <- serial_fgls(y ~ x, data = sim)
vcov(fit)
#>               (Intercept)             x
#> (Intercept)  1.282794e-01 -7.488239e-05
#> x           -7.488239e-05  1.369205e-03
vcov(fit, type = "naive")
#>               (Intercept)             x
#> (Intercept)  1.282722e-01 -8.898623e-05
#> x           -8.898623e-05  1.341769e-03
confint(fit)
#>                 2.5 %   97.5 %
#> (Intercept) 0.4984541 1.902420
#> x           0.9078455 1.052894
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1)), interval = "confidence")
#>         fit        lwr       upr
#> 1 0.2200675 -0.4860593 0.9261944
#> 2 1.2004371  0.4984541 1.9024201
#> 3 2.1808067  1.4754950 2.8861183
head(residuals(fit, type = "innovations"))
#>          2          3          4          5          6          7 
#> -0.8577166  1.5184545  0.2807810 -0.8097611  0.4004779  0.7147435 
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 199
